# ngpel Project Conventions

ngpel is the frontend sister of Archipel: an Nx monorepo of published Angular libraries `@pixel-brewery/ngpel-<name>`.
Sibling product and library repositories are **read-only references**. Never modify them from this workspace.

## Workspace layout

```
libs/<name>/
  package.json          name, sideEffects:false, peerDependencies (+peerDependenciesMeta.optional), ngpel:{category,layer}
  ng-package.json       primary entry (lib.entryFile src/index.ts, dest ./dist)
  <entry>/ng-package.json   one marker directory per secondary entry point; its entryFile points at ../src/<entry>/index.ts
  project.json          tags [lib, layer:N]; targets build-ng (@nx/angular:package), build (post-build), typecheck, test, docs
  tsconfig.json / tsconfig.lib.json (partial-Ivy) / tsconfig.spec.json
  vitest.config.mts     jsdom, explicit resolve.alias for every ngpel specifier the package uses
  eslint.config.mjs     root config + @nx/dependency-checks
  README.md, CHANGELOG.md (generated by nx release)
  src/                  ALL code lives here
    index.ts            primary barrel — one public export per file below it
    test-setup.ts       the package's single test setup
    <entry>/index.ts    the barrel of each secondary entry point
.docs/packages/<name>/index.md (required, rendered) + api/ (generated)
```

## Layering

- Project tag `layer:N`; a project may depend only on projects of a strictly lower layer. `core` and `mvp` (layer 0) import nothing from ngpel; `forms` and `router` are layer 1, `ui` is layer 2.
- Mosaik (`@pixel-brewery/mosaik-elements-angular`, `-foundation`), `@angular/cdk` and the CodeMirror packages are **optional peers of `ui` only**. No other package may import Mosaik or CodeMirror; `tools/postbuild-package.mjs` enforces it.
- `@pixel-brewery/mosaik-themes` ships SCSS only and stays a devDependency: `ui` sets `inlineStyleLanguage: 'scss'`, so the theme mixins are compiled into the published stylesheet.
- Internal dependencies are declared as `peerDependencies` on `@pixel-brewery/ngpel-<dep>` (fixed release group keeps versions aligned).

## Entry points

- A secondary entry point earns its place only when a consumer would import it on its own and would otherwise pay for code it never uses; everything else belongs in the primary entry point.
- Reserved subpath: `./rx`. Single-segment only. There is no `./testing` entry point: ngpel ships no test doubles, and a helper only one package's specs need lives in the spec that uses it.
- ng-packagr generates `exports`; never hand-edit `exports`/`typesVersions` in `package.json`.
- Every entry point needs a `tsconfig.base.json` path (`@pixel-brewery/ngpel-<name>/<entry>` → `libs/<name>/src/<entry>/index.ts`) and a vitest alias; both are generated.
- A file must never import its own entry point's specifier: ng-packagr rejects that as a circular entry point. Use a relative path inside an entry point and the package specifier across entry points.
- Angular resolves interface-typed collaborators through the `useFactory` of the `@Injectable` decorator, because an interface carries no runtime token.

## Lockstep checklist — new entry point

1. Add the entry to `tools/packages.json` (`entryPoints.<entry>: [peers]`).
2. Run `node tools/scaffold-packages.mjs <name>` (creates `<entry>/ng-package.json`, `src/<entry>/index.ts`, syncs `tsconfig.base.json` and the vitest aliases).
3. Add the peer to `package.json` `peerDependencies` (and `peerDependenciesMeta.optional` when it only backs that entry).
4. Add the prose to `tools/docs-content.mjs` and run `node tools/render-package-docs.mjs <name>` (rewrites `README.md` and `.docs/packages/<name>/index.md`).
5. `yarn nx build <name>` and inspect `libs/<name>/dist/package.json` `exports`.

## Lockstep checklist — new package

1. Add the package to `tools/packages.json` (name, layer, category, description, dependsOn, entryPoints).
2. Run `node tools/scaffold-packages.mjs <name>`.
3. Fill `src/` and its specs, add the prose to `tools/docs-content.mjs` and run `node tools/render-package-docs.mjs <name>`.
4. `yarn nx run <name>:build`, `:test`, `:lint`, `:typecheck`, `:docs`.

## Source conventions

See `frontend-coding-standards.instructions.md` and `viewpresenter-behaviors.instructions.md`:
one public export per file, `I`-prefixed interfaces, `_`-prefixed private fields, `#region Fields/Ctor/Properties/Methods`,
TSDoc on public members, standalone components with inline templates and inline styles, signals, `inject()`.
Selector prefix is `ngp` (`[ngpCommand]`, `ngp-widget-summary`, `ngpBytes`) — and so are CSS custom properties,
animation names and `data-` attributes.

Specs run just in time, and the JIT compiler never sees an `input()` initialiser: `ComponentRef.setInput` and a
parent template binding both fail silently. Substitute the field with a signal the spec owns, before the first
change detection. Mosaik's runtime bundle cannot load outside a browser build, so a spec that touches a Mosaik
control mocks the module with `vi.mock`.
